misprints.note: Full stop instead of comma before the termination number.
Acute instead of grave on αὐτό before another word (in Abstraktion). The Abstrakt entry just above prints αὐτὸ correctly.
The print shows an acute and a rough breathing on ω. The usual form in εἰ γὰρ ὡς ὤφελον is ὡς, unaccented. The two marks are also set in an odd order (acute left, breathing right).
The numeral 18 is printed with an acute on η, not a numeral keraia. Kept as printed.

uncertain.note: The two marks over ω are small. They read as acute plus rough breathing, but they might be a broken rough breathing alone (ὡς).
The t of utan is broken in print and looks like 'ucan'. Transcribed as utan.

In this roman fount n often looks like u at 450 dpi (also 'f. ngn' in 0005_06). Read as ngn, but the first and last letters here look closed at the bottom, so turned sorts ('ugu', 'ngu') cannot be ruled out.
